name: Christopher Waller
title: Economic Outlook — remarks at the Council on Foreign Relations
headline: Waller leans toward a 25bp hike in December and would back 50bp if October CPI comes in hot.
bullets: Growth: real GDP tracking ~2.6% in Q4; consumer spending has not slowed as he expected in the summer.
Labour: payroll gains of ~180k/month and unemployment back at 4.0% — 'no sign of the cracks I was worried about'.
Inflation: core PCE stuck near 3.1% y/y; services ex-housing re-accelerating, tariff pass-through broader than assumed.
Expectations: 5y5y breakevens up ~20bp since September — 'not a level I'm comfortable ignoring'.
Policy stance: current setting 'only mildly restrictive, if at all'; sees a 25bp hike on 9 Dec as the base case.
Reaction function: a hot October core CPI (≥0.4% m/m) would make him argue for 50bp.
Risks: skewed to more persistent inflation; downside growth risk from tighter financial conditions seen as manageable.
rates_read: Supports the hawkish front end — {dec} priced for 9 Dec and {jan} cumulative by Jan; a hot CPI print opens the door to a full 25bp+ in Dec.

name: Tom Barkin
voting: Doesn't vote in next FOMC but votes in 2027
title: Navigating Uncertainty — Richmond Fed Economic Outlook Forum
headline: Barkin says the Fed should move with care: inflation risk argues for firmer policy, but he wants more data before committing to a hike.
bullets: Growth: business contacts report steady demand; capex plans firming outside of interest-sensitive sectors.
Labour: hiring 'measured but resilient'; firms reluctant to lay off after recent shortages.
Inflation: price-setters again comfortable passing through cost increases; sees core stuck above 3%.
Policy stance: 'open to tightening' but prefers to see Oct CPI and Nov payrolls before December.
Pace: favours 25bp steps if action is needed; sees little case for 50bp.
Risks: two-sided — sticky inflation vs. a sharper consumer slowdown if real incomes compress.
rates_read: Validates current pricing rather than adding to it — {dec} for 9 Dec / {jan} by Jan looks fair to him; curve likely range-bound into CPI.
